paras: The Barwick whitecap raid was a night attack by a band of disguised whitecaps on Black residents near Barwick, Georgia, on or about Friday, March 6, 1903. The band beat two men and ordered them out of the state, chased a third, and fired into a house, fatally wounding a boy. The reports stressed that the victims were "respectable negroes" and that no reason for the attack was known.

According to a dispatch from Quitman dated March 9, word of the raid reached that town that day, and the attack had taken place "last Friday." The whitecaps entered the house of Charles Lammons, whose name the Savannah Morning News gave as "Hammons," claiming to have a warrant for him and his son. They took the two men into the woods, beat them severely, and gave them forty-eight hours to leave the state.

The band next tried to take Lee Wright, who outran them and hid in the swamp all night. Finally the whitecaps fired into the house of Scott Wilson, "fatally wounding his boy," whose name was not given. The attackers were disguised, and none of them was recognized.
No report of arrests, an inquest or a trial appears in the coverage, and no later report confirms the boy's death or names him.

The Savannah Morning News carried the Quitman dispatch on March 10 under the headline "Whitecaps Whipped Negroes Near Barwick," adding that Wright "gave them leg ball" before escaping. A rewritten version headed "Work of Disguised Whitecaps" and dated only "a few days ago" ran on the front page of the Bamberg Herald in South Carolina on March 12.

The Savannah Tribune, a Black weekly, printed the same syndicated item word for word on its front page on March 14, among unrelated wire news and without comment. Both versions described the victims as "respectable negroes" and said no reason was known for the attack, so the white and Black papers that carried the story gave the same account.

reader.title: Barwick whitecap raid
bases: A disguised band of 'whitecaps' seized and whipped two Black men, ordered them out of the state, chased a third man and fired into a fourth man's house (A1, A3).

The band of disguised whitecaps, claiming a warrant it did not lawfully hold, fired into Scott Wilson's house, 'fatally wounding his boy' (A1, A3); the band's size is not given and the boy's death is reported only as a fatal wound, with no later confirmation.
Both versions trace to one report that 'reached Quitman' on Monday, March 9: the Morning News dispatch (A1) and a syndicated rewrite of it (A2, A3); no independent or follow-up report was found.

accounts.label: Quitman dispatch
accounts.gist: Dated March 9, it places the raid 'last Friday' near Barwick and gives the name as Charles Hammons; the victims were 'respectable negroes' and no reason was known.

accounts.label: Syndicated rewrite
accounts.gist: The same account, dated only 'a few days ago', with the name Charles Lammons, run in a South Carolina weekly and in the Savannah Tribune.

framing.detail: The Morning News headed it 'Whitecaps Whipped Negroes Near Barwick' and repeated that the victims were 'respectable negroes' with no reason known for the attack.
The Bamberg Herald ran the syndicated 'Work of Disguised Whitecaps' item on its front page.
The Savannah Tribune printed the same syndicated item on page 1 among other wire news, without comment.

conflicts.note: Likely a typesetting or transcription variant of one name; neither version is clearly better evidence.
Not a contradiction; the dated dispatch is the more precise.
